title: Prompt engineering help - how to get better facial expressions, especially when holding weapons
author: NChSh
selftext: I am attempting to make a SRPG type game and when I am making the sprites, if they are holding a weapon the AI almost always makes them scowling in some way no matter how I write the prompt.  I have tried mainly PixelLab but a few other things as well.  I was referencing this to Claude and they suggest that because I am putting words like "weapon" or "sword" in the prompt at all, it is reverting to negative or threatening emotions, like it ties it together.  Has anyone had to deal with this?  I want to have like heroic characters and they are almost always coming out very menacingly.  I can eventually get it on rerolls but it ends up taking way longer to get it to come out right.

comments.author: ArtificialBeingsInc
comments.body:
If your PixelLab setup has Inpaint, a two-pass test might save rerolls: first make the hero with the expression you want (“relaxed brows, open eyes, small smile”), then mask the hand/weapon area and add the sword, keeping the face outside the mask. PixelLab’s docs use adding a weapon as an example: [https://www.pixellab.ai/docs/tools/inpaint](https://www.pixellab.ai/docs/tools/inpaint)



If the sword pose is already right, you could try masking the face instead. Check size and credits first: the docs list a 32×32 minimum inpainting size, and Inpaint v3 requires a paid plan and at least 10 generations per use: [https://www.pixellab.ai/docs/tools/inpaint-v3](https://www.pixellab.ai/docs/tools/inpaint-v3)



I haven’t tested this workflow myself, so I’d test one edit before batching. It wouldn’t by itself establish whether the word “sword” caused the scowl.

comments.author: zenmatrix83
comments.body: give ai two exmaples the bad one and the good one, and make it describe both, and then learn what phrasing it needs. No tool will help to you understand whats wrong

comments.author: stolenyourgf
comments.body: Seen this a lot. Words like "sword/weapon/armed" pull the whole face toward aggressive. What usually works: generate the character unarmed first with the expression locked ("calm confident smile, relaxed brows, open eyes"), then add the weapon in a second pass (inpaint just the hand area, or draw/paste the weapon on a separate layer). At 32-64px the expression is really 4-6 pixels anyway: brows tilting down toward the center read as angry, flat or slightly raised brows plus 1px mouth corners turned up read as heroic. Fixing those few pixels by hand is often faster than rerolling 20 times.
